content:
In recent years, Macs have become more and more affordable. With lower starting prices, more RAM and storage per dollar, and the introduction of the MacBook Neo, Apple is for the first time becoming one of the best value options on the market.

Unfortunately, Apple has hiked prices significantly due to ongoing memory shortages. Macs are not quite as attractive as they were a few weeks ago, but there are still some decent deals out there — and if you need a new computer, I still think today's Macs are a good bet relative to the computer market as a whole right now.

MacBook Air

Before the MacBook Neo arrived, the MacBook Air was Apple's entry-level option in its laptop lineup. The arrival of the MacBook Neo makes the MacBook Air's value proposition a little awkward, but if you want a better experience without needing any top-end specs, I'd still call the MacBook Air an exceptionally good laptop.

MagSafe charging, a P3 wide color display, Center Stage for the webcam, and longer battery life are just some of the highlights. It also comes in a 15-inch version, while the MacBook Neo is 13 inches only.

Right now, the entire MacBook Air lineup is discounted as follows:

  • Refurbished M5 MacBook Air: 1TB storage, 16GB RAM — $1,529 at Apple Store

MacBook Neo

This product needs no long explanation — the MacBook Neo is Apple's first budget MacBook, priced at just $699.

It does have trade-offs compared to the MacBook Air above, but it's still a great value at this price. Build quality, display sharpness, and the macOS experience have basically not been sacrificed. Of course, you have to accept a slower A18 Pro chip (though it's honestly not bad at all), fewer ports, and only 8GB of RAM, which is perfectly reasonable at this price point. It also comes in bold color options like Citrus, Blush, and Indigo.

The MacBook Neo currently doesn't have any notable retail discounts, but Apple does sell refurbished models for $100 to $120 less than retail. Apple refurbished units come with the same one-year warranty, an experience that's essentially identical to a new device, with every major component replaced, no scratches, and no battery degradation.

  • MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB RAM — $689 at Amazon ($10 off)
  • MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB RAM, Touch ID — $789 at Amazon ($10 off)
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB RAM — $599 at Apple Store
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB RAM, Touch ID — $679 at Apple Store

MacBook Pro

The MacBook Pro is the flagship of the lineup. You get top-of-the-line specs, but there's one major consideration. Apple is reportedly redesigning its high-end MacBook Pros later this year with OLED, a touchscreen, and a thinner chassis.

However, that redesign will debut only on models with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips — so if you're buying the base M5 model, there's absolutely no problem buying a new MacBook Pro today. And even if you don't care about the redesign at all, the M5 Pro and M5 Max are still excellent new chips.
